title: Geometric Shape Atlas
subtitle: The figures of geometry, from the point and the ray to the solid and the polytope.
intro: Every geometric shape in the corpus decomposition, rendered as a figure and read as a path. The atlas follows the table in the Geometric Shape note: elemental forms first, then curves, planar and curved regions, solids, higher-dimensional polytopes, and arrangements.

families.name: Elemental Shapes
families.essence: The degenerate forms with empty interior in their ambient space.

families.name: One-Dimensional Shapes
families.essence: Curves and the pieces curves are built from.

families.name: Planar Shapes
families.essence: Polygonal and curved regions of the plane.

families.name: Spherical Shapes
families.essence: Figures drawn on a sphere, where angle sums exceed the Euclidean.

families.name: Hyperbolic Shapes
families.essence: Figures drawn in hyperbolic space, where angle sums fall short.

families.name: Solid Shapes
families.essence: Polyhedra, quadric surfaces, and closed surfaces in three dimensions.

families.name: Higher-Dimensional Shapes
families.essence: Polytopes, balls, and spheres beyond three dimensions.

families.name: Shape Arrangements
families.essence: Shapes taken together: compounds, tessellations, and packings.

families.name: Shape Properties
families.essence: Predicates asserted of a shape rather than figures beside it.

roots.label: Geometric Shape
roots.description: The form a figure carries — the orbit of a point set under a declared transformation group, never the figure that represents it.

children.label: Elemental Shapes
children.path: Geometric Shape → Elemental Shapes
children.description: The degenerate family: figure forms with empty interior in their ambient space.

children.label: Point
children.path: Geometric Shape → Elemental Shapes → Point
children.description: The 0-dimensional shape: one point, invariant under every group.

children.label: Line
children.path: Geometric Shape → Elemental Shapes → Line
children.description: A straight shape with no endpoints — degenerate in $\mathbb{R}^2$, since it encloses nothing; see Line.

children.label: Line Segment
children.path: Geometric Shape → Elemental Shapes → Line Segment
children.description: The part of a line between two points: the elementary edge of every polygon.

children.label: Ray
children.path: Geometric Shape → Elemental Shapes → Ray
children.description: A half-line — one endpoint, unbounded in one direction.

children.label: Plane
children.path: Geometric Shape → Elemental Shapes → Plane
children.description: The 2-D elemental shape spanning all of $\mathbb{R}^3$; see Plane.

children.label: Hyperplane
children.path: Geometric Shape → Elemental Shapes → Hyperplane
children.description: The $(n-1)$-dimensional flat that slices an $n$-space; see Hyperplane.

children.label: One-Dimensional Shapes
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes
children.description: The family of shapes of dimension one: curves and the pieces curves are built from.

children.label: Curve
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve
children.description: The image of a continuous interval map into space — the generic 1-D shape.

children.label: Simple Curve
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Simple Curve
children.description: A curve with no self-intersection; its parameterization is injective.

children.label: Closed Curve
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Closed Curve
children.description: A curve whose endpoints coincide, bounding a region of the plane.

children.label: Jordan Curve
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Jordan Curve
children.description: A simple closed curve; by the Jordan theorem it cuts the plane into exactly an inside and an outside.

children.label: Space Curve
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Space Curve
children.description: A curve lying in no single plane — where knot and link shapes live.

children.label: Unknot
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Space Curve → Unknot
children.description: The trivial embedding: a closed curve bounding an embedded disk.

children.label: Trefoil Knot
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Space Curve → Trefoil Knot
children.description: The simplest nontrivial knot — three crossings, and the $(2,3)$ torus knot.

children.label: Figure-Eight Knot
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Space Curve → Figure-Eight Knot
children.description: The only knot with four crossings; amphichiral, unlike the trefoil.

children.label: Hopf Link
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Space Curve → Hopf Link
children.description: Two circles linked once — the simplest link, and a two-component shape.

children.label: Conic Section
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Conic Section
children.description: The plane section of a cone: one family, and the shape of every orbit under an inverse-square force.

children.label: Parabola
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Conic Section → Parabola
children.description: The conic of eccentricity one: points equidistant from a focus and a directrix.

children.label: Hyperbola
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Conic Section → Hyperbola
children.description: The conic of eccentricity above one: two branches, and the shape of unbounded orbits.

children.label: Degenerate Conic
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Conic Section → Degenerate Conic
children.description: A point, a line, or a pair of lines: the section when the plane passes through the apex.

children.label: Cycloid
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Cycloid
children.description: The roulette of a point on a circle rolling along a line — the curve of quickest descent.

children.label: Epicycloid
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Cycloid → Epicycloid
children.description: A point on a circle rolling outside a fixed circle; the cardioid is the equal-radius case.

children.label: Hypocycloid
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Cycloid → Hypocycloid
children.description: A point on a circle rolling inside a fixed circle.

children.label: Astroid
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Cycloid → Hypocycloid → Astroid
children.description: The four-cusp hypocycloid, $x^{2/3} + y^{2/3} = a^{2/3}$ — the envelope of a ladder sliding down a wall.

children.label: Deltoid
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Cycloid → Hypocycloid → Deltoid
children.description: The three-cusp hypocycloid, with three-fold symmetry and a Steiner-curve reading.

children.label: Epitrochoid
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Cycloid → Epitrochoid
children.description: The epicycloid with the traced point moved off the rolling circle — the spirograph curve.

children.label: Hypotrochoid
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Cycloid → Hypotrochoid
children.description: The hypocycloid with the traced point moved off the rolling circle.

children.label: Catenary
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Catenary
children.description: The shape a hanging chain takes — the hyperbolic cosine, and the funicular form of an arch.

children.label: Tractrix
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Tractrix
children.description: The curve whose tangent segment to its axis keeps constant length — the path of a dragged point.

children.label: Clothoid
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Clothoid
children.description: The Euler spiral: curvature proportional to arclength, so a vehicle enters a circular arc without a curvature jump.

children.label: Lemniscate
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Lemniscate
children.description: The figure-eight curve on which the product of distances to two foci is constant.

children.label: Lemniscate of Bernoulli
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Lemniscate → Lemniscate of Bernoulli
children.description: The $\infty$-shaped case: the inverse of a hyperbola in its own circle.

children.label: Lemniscate of Gerono
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Lemniscate → Lemniscate of Gerono
children.description: The looped quartic $x^4 = a^2(x^2 - y^2)$ — a figure-eight without the Bernoulli geometry.

children.label: Cassini Oval
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Cassini Oval
children.description: Points whose distances to two foci have a constant product; it passes through the lemniscate at the critical value.

children.label: Lissajous Curve
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Lissajous Curve
children.description: The path of a point under two perpendicular harmonic motions: closed exactly when the frequency ratio is rational.

children.label: Rose Curve
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Rose Curve
children.description: The rhodonea $r = a\cos(k\theta)$: $k$ petals for odd $k$, $2k$ for even.

children.label: Superellipse
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Superellipse
children.description: The Lamé curve $|x/a|^n + |y/b|^n = 1$: an ellipse at $n = 2$, a rectangle in the limit.

children.label: Witch of Agnesi
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Witch of Agnesi
children.description: The versed-sine cubic $y = 8a^3/(x^2 + 4a^2)$: one inflection, two asymptotes.

children.label: Cissoid of Diocles
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Cissoid of Diocles
children.description: The curve built from a circle and a tangent that solves the doubling of the cube.

children.label: Conchoid of Nicomedes
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Conchoid of Nicomedes
children.description: A line's points displaced by a fixed distance along rays from a pole — the curve behind angle trisection.

children.label: Folium of Descartes
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Folium of Descartes
children.description: The looped cubic $x^3 + y^3 = 3axy$, with a node at the origin and an oblique asymptote.

children.label: Strophoid
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Strophoid
children.description: The looped curve traced by reflecting a pencil of lines through a fixed point about a given line.

children.label: Elliptic Curve
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Curve → Elliptic Curve
children.description: A nonsingular cubic of genus one — a curve that is also an abelian group under its chord-and-tangent law.

children.label: Polygonal Chain
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Polygonal Chain
children.description: A finite sequence of segments joined end to end: open it is a polyline, closed it is a polygon.

children.label: Arc
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Arc
children.description: A connected piece of a curve, cut from a circle or from any other curve.

children.label: Circle
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Circle
children.description: The points at one distance from a centre — a closed curve; its filled interior is the Disk.

children.label: Spiral
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Spiral
children.description: A curve winding about a centre with monotonically changing radius (Archimedean, logarithmic).

children.label: Archimedean Spiral
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Spiral → Archimedean Spiral
children.description: Radius proportional to angle: equal spacing between successive turns.

children.label: Logarithmic Spiral
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Spiral → Logarithmic Spiral
children.description: Radius growing geometrically with angle — self-similar, and the shell and galaxy form.

children.label: Spiral of Theodorus
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Spiral → Spiral of Theodorus
children.description: Right triangles of leg $1$ laid end to end, with hypotenuses $\sqrt{n}$.

children.label: Helix
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Helix
children.description: A curve winding around an axis at constant radius and constant pitch.

children.label: Conical Spiral
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Helix → Conical Spiral
children.description: A helix of linearly shrinking radius — the string wound on a cone.

children.label: Spline
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Spline
children.description: A piecewise-polynomial curve fixed by control points — the computational representative of a smooth curve.

children.label: Bézier Curve
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Spline → Bézier Curve
children.description: A Bernstein-basis curve determined by control points, contained in their convex hull.

children.label: B-Spline
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Spline → B-Spline
children.description: A locally supported piecewise polynomial: moving one control point changes only a neighbourhood.

children.label: NURBS
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Spline → NURBS
children.description: A rational B-spline: conics and free-form curves in one control-point representation.

children.label: Fractal Curve
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Fractal Curve
children.description: A curve of non-integer dimension, self-similar at every scale.

children.label: Koch Curve
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Fractal Curve → Koch Curve
children.description: Each segment replaced by a four-segment bump; dimension $\log 4 / \log 3$.

children.label: Dragon Curve
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Fractal Curve → Dragon Curve
children.description: The paper-folding curve, whose copies tile the plane without overlap.

children.label: Hilbert Curve
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Fractal Curve → Hilbert Curve
children.description: A space-filling curve whose limit is the whole square — the classical dimension-breaking shape.

children.label: Lévy C Curve
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Fractal Curve → Lévy C Curve
children.description: A self-similar curve built from a right isosceles step; dimension $2$ in the limit.

children.label: Minkowski Sausage
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Fractal Curve → Minkowski Sausage
children.description: A segment replaced by eight-segment bumps; dimension $\log 8 / \log 4 = 1.5$.

children.label: Moore Curve
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Fractal Curve → Moore Curve
children.description: The Hilbert curve closed into a loop, filling the square in one continuous stroke.

children.label: Sierpiński Curve
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Fractal Curve → Sierpiński Curve
children.description: A closed space-filling curve whose limit is the Sierpiński triangle.

children.label: Gosper Curve
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Fractal Curve → Gosper Curve
children.description: The flowsnake: a hexagonal space-filling curve, the boundary of the Gosper island.

children.label: Peano Curve
children.path: Geometric Shape → One-Dimensional Shapes → Fractal Curve → Peano Curve
children.description: The first space-filling curve: a continuous map of the interval onto the square.

children.label: Planar Shapes
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes
children.description: The family of 2-D shapes: polygonal and curved regions of the plane.

children.label: Polygon
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon
children.description: A simple closed polygonal chain with the region it bounds; see Polygon.

children.label: Triangle
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Triangle
children.description: The 3-sided polygon — the simplest rigid shape, and the unit of every triangulation; see Triangle.

children.label: Equilateral Triangle
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Triangle → Equilateral Triangle
children.description: Three equal sides and three $60^\circ$ angles; regular, and a similarity class of its own.

children.label: Isosceles Triangle
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Triangle → Isosceles Triangle
children.description: Two equal sides and two equal base angles — one axis of symmetry.

children.label: Scalene Triangle
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Triangle → Scalene Triangle
children.description: No equal sides, no symmetry.

children.label: Right Triangle
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Triangle → Right Triangle
children.description: One $90^\circ$ angle; its sides satisfy $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$ (Pythagorean Theorem).

children.label: Acute Triangle
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Triangle → Acute Triangle
children.description: All angles below $90^\circ$; the circumcentre falls inside the triangle.

children.label: Obtuse Triangle
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Triangle → Obtuse Triangle
children.description: One angle above $90^\circ$; the circumcentre falls outside.

children.label: Isosceles Right Triangle
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Triangle → Isosceles Right Triangle
children.description: The $45^\circ$–$45^\circ$–$90^\circ$ shape, with sides in ratio $1 : 1 : \sqrt{2}$.

children.label: Golden Triangle
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Triangle → Golden Triangle
children.description: Isosceles with leg-to-base ratio $\varphi$; its angles are $72^\circ$ and $36^\circ$, and it repeats inside the pentagon.

children.label: 30-60-90 Triangle
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Triangle → 30-60-90 Triangle
children.description: The half-equilateral: sides in ratio $1 : \sqrt{3} : 2$, the triangle of every drafting set.

children.label: Heronian Triangle
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Triangle → Heronian Triangle
children.description: Integer sides and integer area — the $3$-$4$-$5$ triangle is the smallest.

children.label: Equable Triangle
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Triangle → Equable Triangle
children.description: Perimeter equal to area: a family cut out by $r = 2$ in the inradius relation.

children.label: Golden Gnomon
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Triangle → Golden Gnomon
children.description: The obtuse isosceles triangle of angles $36^\circ$, $36^\circ$, $108^\circ$ — the golden triangle's companion in the pentagon.

children.label: Quadrilateral
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Quadrilateral
children.description: The 4-sided polygon; unlike the triangle kinds, its kinds form a lattice rather than a chain.

children.label: Rectangle
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Quadrilateral → Rectangle
children.description: All four angles right — the constraint laid on angles.

children.label: Square
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Quadrilateral → Rectangle → Square
children.description: The rectangle with equal sides: one of the two lattice intersections, typed here under its angle constraint.

children.label: Parallelogram
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Quadrilateral → Parallelogram
children.description: Both pairs of opposite sides parallel — the minimal parallelism constraint.

children.label: Rhombus
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Quadrilateral → Parallelogram → Rhombus
children.description: A parallelogram with equal sides; its angles stay free.

children.label: Square
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Quadrilateral → Parallelogram → Rhombus → Square
children.description: The rhombus with a right angle — the second occurrence of Square, now under its side constraint.

children.label: Trapezoid
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Quadrilateral → Trapezoid
children.description: Exactly one pair of parallel sides.

children.label: Isosceles Trapezoid
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Quadrilateral → Trapezoid → Isosceles Trapezoid
children.description: A trapezoid with equal legs: cyclic, with equal base angles.

children.label: Right Trapezoid
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Quadrilateral → Trapezoid → Right Trapezoid
children.description: A trapezoid with two right angles — the constraint that makes one leg the height.

children.label: Kite
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Quadrilateral → Kite
children.description: Two pairs of adjacent equal sides, hence orthogonal diagonals.

children.label: Dart
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Quadrilateral → Kite → Dart
children.description: The concave kite: one reflex angle, and the arrowhead form.

children.label: Trapezium
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Quadrilateral → Trapezium
children.description: The general quadrilateral with no parallel sides — the shape the other kinds specialize.

children.label: Cyclic Quadrilateral
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Quadrilateral → Cyclic Quadrilateral
children.description: All four vertices on one circle; opposite angles sum to $180^\circ$.

children.label: Tangential Quadrilateral
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Quadrilateral → Tangential Quadrilateral
children.description: A circle tangent to all four sides; Pitot's relation $a + c = b + d$ holds.

children.label: Antiparallelogram
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Quadrilateral → Antiparallelogram
children.description: The self-crossing quadrilateral with equal opposite sides — a linkage, not a simple polygon.

children.label: Orthodiagonal Quadrilateral
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Quadrilateral → Orthodiagonal Quadrilateral
children.description: Diagonals perpendicular — the class the kite and the rhombus both fall in.

children.label: Equidiagonal Quadrilateral
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Quadrilateral → Equidiagonal Quadrilateral
children.description: Diagonals of equal length — the class the isosceles trapezoid and the rectangle fall in.

children.label: Bicentric Quadrilateral
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Quadrilateral → Bicentric Quadrilateral
children.description: Both cyclic and tangential: one incircle and one circumcircle.

children.label: Ex-tangential Quadrilateral
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Quadrilateral → Ex-tangential Quadrilateral
children.description: An excircle tangent to all four side lines — the tangential kind read from outside.

children.label: Pentagon
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Pentagon
children.description: 5 sides; its diagonals carry the golden ratio.

children.label: Regular Pentagon
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Pentagon → Regular Pentagon
children.description: Equal sides and angles; its diagonal divides the side in golden section.

children.label: Hexagon
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Hexagon
children.description: 6 sides; the regular form is the only regular polygon that tiles the plane.

children.label: Regular Hexagon
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Hexagon → Regular Hexagon
children.description: Six equilateral triangles about one centre — the honeycomb cell.

children.label: Heptagon
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Heptagon
children.description: 7 sides; the regular form is not constructible with straightedge and compass.

children.label: Octagon
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Octagon
children.description: 8 sides; the regular form arises by cutting the corners of a square.

children.label: Regular Octagon
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Octagon → Regular Octagon
children.description: Equal sides and angles — the stop-sign shape.

children.label: Nonagon
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Nonagon
children.description: 9 sides; constructible only by neusis or with trisection, not by compass and straightedge.

children.label: Decagon
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Decagon
children.description: 10 sides; the decagon's vertex geometry is the pentagon's, scaled.

children.label: Hendecagon
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Hendecagon
children.description: 11 sides — the first regular polygon not constructible with compass and straightedge.

children.label: Dodecagon
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Dodecagon
children.description: 12 sides; the clock face, and a face of several Archimedean solids.

children.label: N-gon
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → N-gon
children.description: The parametric family: $n$ sides, $n$ vertices, interior angles summing to $(n-2)\,180^\circ$.

children.label: Regular Polygon
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Regular Polygon
children.description: All sides and all angles equal — one kind parameterized by side count, not a separate shape per $n$.

children.label: Star Polygon
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Star Polygon
children.description: A self-intersecting polygon whose boundary winds more than once around its centre.

children.label: Pentagram
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Star Polygon → Pentagram
children.description: $\{5/2\}$: the five-point star, and the pentagon's diagonals taken in order.

children.label: Hexagram
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Star Polygon → Hexagram
children.description: $\{6/2\}$: two equilateral triangles superposed — the Star of David.

children.label: Octagram
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Star Polygon → Octagram
children.description: $\{8/3\}$: the eight-pointed star of the octagon's extended sides.

children.label: Heptagram
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Star Polygon → Heptagram
children.description: $\{7/2\}$ and $\{7/3\}$: the seven-point stars, neither constructible with compass and straightedge.

children.label: Enneagram
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Star Polygon → Enneagram
children.description: $\{9/2\}$ and $\{9/4\}$: the nine-point stars, with three-fold symmetry.

children.label: Decagram
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Star Polygon → Decagram
children.description: $\{10/3\}$: the ten-point star, two pentagrams superposed.

children.label: Hendecagram
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Star Polygon → Hendecagram
children.description: $\{11/2\}$ through $\{11/5\}$: the eleven-point stars.

children.label: Dodecagram
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Star Polygon → Dodecagram
children.description: $\{12/5\}$: the twelve-point star, and the star polygon of the dodecagon.

children.label: Degenerate Polygon
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Degenerate Polygon
children.description: Polygons that press on the definition without leaving it.

children.label: Monogon
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Degenerate Polygon → Monogon
children.description: One side and one vertex — admissible only in a widened definition.

children.label: Digon
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Degenerate Polygon → Digon
children.description: Two sides between two vertices — in the plane a lens of two arcs, in spherical geometry a genuine polygon.

children.label: Equilateral Polygon
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Equilateral Polygon
children.description: All sides equal, angles free — the constraint the regular polygon adds to.

children.label: Equiangular Polygon
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Equiangular Polygon
children.description: All angles equal, sides free — the dual constraint.

children.label: Cyclic Polygon
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Cyclic Polygon
children.description: All vertices on one circle — every triangle is cyclic, not every quadrilateral.

children.label: Tangential Polygon
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Tangential Polygon
children.description: A circle tangent to every side — the polygon that has an incircle.

children.label: Apeirogon
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Polygon → Apeirogon
children.description: The infinite-sided polygon: the limit of the $n$-gon, with a vertex at infinity.

children.label: Disk
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Disk
children.description: The closed region bounded by a circle — the circle's filled interior, not the circle itself.

children.label: Semicircle
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Disk → Semicircle
children.description: Half a disk cut by a diameter — the region, distinct from the half-circle curve.

children.label: Crescent
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Disk → Crescent
children.description: The lune between two circular arcs — what remains when one disk is subtracted from another.

children.label: Reuleaux Triangle
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Disk → Reuleaux Triangle
children.description: The curve of constant width on three vertices — a drill bit that cuts a square hole.

children.label: Stadium
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Disk → Stadium
children.description: A rectangle capped by two semicircles — the capsule, and the two-foci distance shape.

children.label: Ellipse
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Ellipse
children.description: The affine image of a circle: points whose distances to two foci sum to a constant.

children.label: Annulus
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Annulus
children.description: The region between two concentric circles — a planar shape with exactly one hole.

children.label: Circular Sector
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Circular Sector
children.description: The wedge of a disk cut out by two radii.

children.label: Circular Segment
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Circular Segment
children.description: The part of a disk cut off by a chord.

children.label: Lens
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Lens
children.description: The intersection of two disks — a curvilinear region bounded by two arcs.

children.label: Cardioid
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Cardioid
children.description: The epicycloid traced by a point on a circle rolling around an equal fixed circle.

children.label: Parabolic Region
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Parabolic Region
children.description: The region between a parabola and a chord — the affine normal form of a planar cap.

children.label: Fractal Region
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Fractal Region
children.description: A planar region whose boundary is self-similar.

children.label: Sierpinski Triangle
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Fractal Region → Sierpinski Triangle
children.description: A triangle with its middle triangle removed at every scale: area zero, dimension $\log 3 / \log 2$.

children.label: Sierpinski Carpet
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Fractal Region → Sierpinski Carpet
children.description: The square analogue: nine sub-squares, the central one removed recursively.

children.label: Koch Snowflake
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Fractal Region → Koch Snowflake
children.description: Three Koch curves on an equilateral triangle: finite area, infinite perimeter.

children.label: Mandelbrot Set
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Fractal Region → Mandelbrot Set
children.description: The set of $c$ for which $z \mapsto z^2 + c$ stays bounded — the parameter plane of the quadratic family.

children.label: Julia Set
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Fractal Region → Julia Set
children.description: The boundary between bounded and escaping orbits for one fixed $c$ — the Mandelbrot set's slice.

children.label: Apollonian Gasket
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Fractal Region → Apollonian Gasket
children.description: The limit of repeatedly inscribing mutually tangent circles — a fractal of circles, not of polygons.

children.label: Cantor Dust
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Fractal Region → Cantor Dust
children.description: The interval with its middle third removed forever: uncountably many points, zero length.

children.label: Vicsek Fractal
children.path: Geometric Shape → Planar Shapes → Fractal Region → Vicsek Fractal
children.description: The cross-shaped self-similar set: five squares, the centre one kept.

children.label: Spherical Shapes
children.path: Geometric Shape → Spherical Shapes
children.description: The family of shapes drawn on a sphere: the non-Euclidean planar figures.

children.label: Spherical Triangle
children.path: Geometric Shape → Spherical Shapes → Spherical Triangle
children.description: Three great-circle arcs: angles summing to more than $180^\circ$, by the spherical excess.

children.label: Spherical Lune
children.path: Geometric Shape → Spherical Shapes → Spherical Lune
children.description: The wedge between two great circles through antipodal points — the spherical sector.

children.label: Spherical Cap
children.path: Geometric Shape → Spherical Shapes → Spherical Cap
children.description: The part of a sphere cut off by a plane — the spherical analogue of a circular segment.

children.label: Spherical Polygon
children.path: Geometric Shape → Spherical Shapes → Spherical Polygon
children.description: A region bounded by great-circle arcs — the spherical analogue of the planar polygon.

children.label: Hyperbolic Shapes
children.path: Geometric Shape → Hyperbolic Shapes
children.description: The family of shapes drawn in hyperbolic space: the planar figures of constant negative curvature.

children.label: Hyperbolic Triangle
children.path: Geometric Shape → Hyperbolic Shapes → Hyperbolic Triangle
children.description: Three geodesics: angles summing to less than $180^\circ$, by the defect.

children.label: Ideal Triangle
children.path: Geometric Shape → Hyperbolic Shapes → Ideal Triangle
children.description: A hyperbolic triangle whose three vertices lie at infinity, with all angles zero.

children.label: Solid Shapes
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes
children.description: The family of 3-D shapes: polyhedra, quadric surfaces, and closed surfaces.

children.label: Polyhedron
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron
children.description: A closed surface of flat polygonal faces — the 3-D counterpart of the polygon.

children.label: Prism
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Prism
children.description: Two congruent parallel faces joined by parallelograms: a product shape, base $\times$ height.

children.label: Rectangular Prism
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Prism → Rectangular Prism
children.description: Six rectangles — the box, and the affine normal form of every parallelepiped.

children.label: Triangular Prism
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Prism → Triangular Prism
children.description: A triangle extruded: five faces, and the dispersing prism of optics.

children.label: Pentagonal Prism
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Prism → Pentagonal Prism
children.description: A pentagon extruded — one of the Archimedean prisms.

children.label: Hexagonal Prism
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Prism → Hexagonal Prism
children.description: A hexagon extruded — the honeycomb cell, and the basalt column.

children.label: Oblique Prism
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Prism → Oblique Prism
children.description: A prism whose lateral edges are not perpendicular to the base: volume unchanged, faces are parallelograms.

children.label: Parallelepiped
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Prism → Parallelepiped
children.description: Six parallelograms — the affine image of the cube, and the 3-D cell of a lattice.

children.label: Rhombohedron
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Prism → Parallelepiped → Rhombohedron
children.description: A parallelepiped on equal edges — the unit cell of the trigonal lattice.

children.label: Pyramid
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Pyramid
children.description: A polygon base with triangular faces meeting at one apex.

children.label: Square Pyramid
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Pyramid → Square Pyramid
children.description: The pyramid over a square — the canonical roof, and half an octahedron.

children.label: Triangular Pyramid
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Pyramid → Triangular Pyramid
children.description: A tetrahedron read as a pyramid over a triangle — the two readings coincide.

children.label: Pentagonal Pyramid
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Pyramid → Pentagonal Pyramid
children.description: A pentagon base with five triangular faces — half an icosahedron.

children.label: Oblique Pyramid
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Pyramid → Oblique Pyramid
children.description: A pyramid whose apex is off the base centre: the slant heights differ.

children.label: Frustum
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Frustum
children.description: A pyramid or cone cut parallel to its base — the shape of a truncated solid.

children.label: Antiprism
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Antiprism
children.description: Two parallel $n$-gons joined by a band of triangles pointing alternately up and down.

children.label: Platonic Solid
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Platonic Solid
children.description: The five regular convex polyhedra: one face kind, and the same vertex figure at every corner.

children.label: Tetrahedron
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Platonic Solid → Tetrahedron
children.description: 4 equilateral triangles; self-dual, and the 3-simplex.

children.label: Disphenoid
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Platonic Solid → Tetrahedron → Disphenoid
children.description: The isosceles tetrahedron: congruent faces, and the only tetrahedron with a symmetry axis through edge midpoints.

children.label: Trirectangular Tetrahedron
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Platonic Solid → Tetrahedron → Trirectangular Tetrahedron
children.description: Three right angles at one vertex — the corner of a box, and the de Gua analogue of the right triangle.

children.label: Orthoscheme
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Platonic Solid → Tetrahedron → Orthoscheme
children.description: A tetrahedron whose faces are right triangles — the simplex that tiles space by reflection.

children.label: Cube
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Platonic Solid → Cube
children.description: 6 squares, dual to the octahedron — the 3-D face of the hypercube.

children.label: Octahedron
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Platonic Solid → Octahedron
children.description: 8 equilateral triangles — the 3-D cross-polytope.

children.label: Dodecahedron
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Platonic Solid → Dodecahedron
children.description: 12 regular pentagons, with a triangular vertex figure.

children.label: Icosahedron
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Platonic Solid → Icosahedron
children.description: 20 equilateral triangles, dual to the dodecahedron.

children.label: Archimedean Solid
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Archimedean Solid
children.description: Convex polyhedra with regular faces of more than one kind — thirteen of them.

children.label: Johnson Solid
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Johnson Solid
children.description: Convex polyhedra with regular but non-uniform faces — ninety-two of them.

children.label: Deltahedron
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Deltahedron
children.description: Polyhedra whose faces are all equilateral triangles; eight are strictly convex.

children.label: Bipyramid
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Bipyramid
children.description: Two pyramids joined at their base — the dual of the prism.

children.label: Trapezohedron
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Trapezohedron
children.description: The dual of the antiprism: kite faces, and the crystal form of quartz.

children.label: Prismatoid
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Prismatoid
children.description: A polyhedron whose vertices lie in two parallel planes — the family that contains prisms, pyramids, and frusta.

children.label: Cupola
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Cupola
children.description: A polygon joined to a rotated copy by a band of triangles and squares — the dome slice.

children.label: Rotunda
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Rotunda
children.description: A cupola continued to a half-rotated base — the pentagonal rotunda is half an icosidodecahedron.

children.label: Wedge
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Wedge
children.description: A triangular prism cut obliquely — the ramp, and the simplest non-prismatic solid.

children.label: Sphenoid
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Sphenoid
children.description: A tetrahedron with four congruent isosceles faces — the disphenoid under its crystallographic name.

children.label: Zonohedron
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Zonohedron
children.description: A convex polyhedron whose faces are centrally symmetric — the Minkowski sum of segments.

children.label: Toroidal Polyhedron
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Toroidal Polyhedron
children.description: A polyhedron with a hole: the torus form built from flat faces.

children.label: Kepler–Poinsot Solid
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Kepler–Poinsot Solid
children.description: The four regular star polyhedra: regular faces, self-intersecting, and non-convex.

children.label: Small Stellated Dodecahedron
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Kepler–Poinsot Solid → Small Stellated Dodecahedron
children.description: Twelve pentagrams meeting five at each vertex.

children.label: Great Dodecahedron
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Kepler–Poinsot Solid → Great Dodecahedron
children.description: Twelve intersecting pentagons, with the icosahedron's vertex arrangement.

children.label: Great Stellated Dodecahedron
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Kepler–Poinsot Solid → Great Stellated Dodecahedron
children.description: Twelve pentagrams on the icosahedron's vertices.

children.label: Great Icosahedron
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Kepler–Poinsot Solid → Great Icosahedron
children.description: Twenty intersecting triangles — the last of the four.

children.label: Catalan Solid
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Polyhedron → Catalan Solid
children.description: The thirteen duals of the Archimedean solids: face-transitive, with regular vertices.

children.label: Quadric Surface
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Quadric Surface
children.description: The zero set of a quadratic form: one family, five affine shapes.

children.label: Sphere
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Quadric Surface → Sphere
children.description: The points at constant distance from a centre — the affine normal form of every ellipsoid.

children.label: Hemisphere
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Quadric Surface → Sphere → Hemisphere
children.description: Half a sphere cut by a great circle — the dome, with one flat face and one curved.

children.label: Ellipsoid
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Quadric Surface → Ellipsoid
children.description: The affine image of a sphere: three semi-axes, no edges and no vertices.

children.label: Paraboloid
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Quadric Surface → Paraboloid
children.description: The bowl $z = x^2 + y^2$, or its saddle variant — one equation, two shapes.

children.label: Hyperboloid
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Quadric Surface → Hyperboloid
children.description: One- or two-sheeted, and ruled: the shape of cooling towers and of quadric reconstruction.

children.label: Cylinder
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Quadric Surface → Cylinder
children.description: A circle carried along a line ($x^2 + y^2 = r^2$): translation-invariant, so one principal curvature vanishes.

children.label: Right Circular Cylinder
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Quadric Surface → Cylinder → Right Circular Cylinder
children.description: The axis perpendicular to the base: one principal curvature zero, the other $1/r$.

children.label: Oblique Cylinder
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Quadric Surface → Cylinder → Oblique Cylinder
children.description: A cylinder sheared off the perpendicular — the same volume, elliptic cross-sections.

children.label: Elliptic Cylinder
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Quadric Surface → Cylinder → Elliptic Cylinder
children.description: An ellipse extruded along its axis — the affine image of the circular cylinder.

children.label: Cone
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Quadric Surface → Cone
children.description: The lines through a point and a conic — the shape whose plane sections are the conic shapes.

children.label: Right Circular Cone
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Quadric Surface → Cone → Right Circular Cone
children.description: The axis perpendicular to the base circle — the cone whose sections are the conics.

children.label: Oblique Cone
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Quadric Surface → Cone → Oblique Cone
children.description: An apex off the base centre: the sections are still conics, the symmetry is gone.

children.label: Double Cone
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Quadric Surface → Cone → Double Cone
children.description: Two cones apex to apex — the surface whose plane sections give every conic.

children.label: Hyperbolic Paraboloid
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Quadric Surface → Hyperbolic Paraboloid
children.description: The saddle $z = x^2 - y^2$: doubly ruled, with negative Gaussian curvature at every point.

children.label: Monkey Saddle
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Quadric Surface → Monkey Saddle
children.description: The cubic saddle $z = x^3 - 3xy^2$: three hills and three valleys, not a quadric.

children.label: Torus
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Torus
children.description: The surface of a ring: genus one, $\chi = 0$, and the standard closed surface with a handle.

children.label: Spindle Torus
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Torus → Spindle Torus
children.description: The self-intersecting case: the tube radius exceeds the ring radius, and the inner surface turns inside out.

children.label: Horn Torus
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Torus → Horn Torus
children.description: The critical case: tube radius equal to ring radius, closing to a single point at the centre.

children.label: Solid Torus
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Torus → Solid Torus
children.description: The torus together with the volume it encloses — the 3-D shape whose boundary is the torus.

children.label: Möbius Strip
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Möbius Strip
children.description: A one-sided, non-orientable surface with boundary — the canonical non-orientable shape.

children.label: Klein Bottle
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Klein Bottle
children.description: A closed non-orientable surface, embeddable only in four dimensions.

children.label: Surface of Revolution
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Surface of Revolution
children.description: The surface swept by a plane curve rotated about an axis — spheres, tori, and cones as cases.

children.label: Fractal Solid
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Fractal Solid
children.description: A 3-D self-similar body of non-integer dimension.

children.label: Menger Sponge
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Fractal Solid → Menger Sponge
children.description: The Sierpinski carpet lifted into the cube: volume zero, surface area infinite.

children.label: Sierpiński Tetrahedron
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Fractal Solid → Sierpiński Tetrahedron
children.description: The tetrahedron with its central octahedron removed recursively — the 3-D Sierpiński form.

children.label: Ruled Surface
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Ruled Surface
children.description: A surface swept by a moving line — the general family of which cylinders and hyperboloids are cases.

children.label: Developable Surface
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Ruled Surface → Developable Surface
children.description: A ruled surface of zero Gaussian curvature: it unrolls onto the plane without stretching.

children.label: Minimal Surface
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Minimal Surface
children.description: A surface of zero mean curvature — the soap-film shape that minimizes area for its boundary.

children.label: Catenoid
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Minimal Surface → Catenoid
children.description: The surface of revolution of a catenary: the only minimal surface of revolution besides the plane.

children.label: Helicoid
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Minimal Surface → Helicoid
children.description: The ruled minimal surface — the only ruled minimal surface besides the plane, and the catenoid's isometric twin.

children.label: Enneper Surface
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Minimal Surface → Enneper Surface
children.description: A self-intersecting minimal surface with no straight lines and full symmetry.

children.label: Scherk Surface
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Minimal Surface → Scherk Surface
children.description: A doubly periodic minimal surface: a family of saddles stacked in a lattice.

children.label: Gyroid
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Minimal Surface → Gyroid
children.description: A triply periodic minimal surface with no straight lines — the photonic-crystal and membrane form.

children.label: Pseudosphere
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Pseudosphere
children.description: The tractroid: the surface of revolution of a tractrix, with constant negative curvature — the hyperbolic plane's embedded patch.

children.label: Boy's Surface
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Boy's Surface
children.description: An immersion of the real projective plane in 3-space, with three-fold symmetry and one triple point.

children.label: Roman Surface
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Roman Surface
children.description: Steiner's immersion of the projective plane: six cross-caps on the coordinate axes.

children.label: Cross-Cap
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Cross-Cap
children.description: The local model of a projective-plane immersion: two sheets meeting along a segment.

children.label: Real Projective Plane
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Real Projective Plane
children.description: The quotient of the sphere by antipodal points — closed, non-orientable, and not embeddable in 3-space.

children.label: Dini's Surface
children.path: Geometric Shape → Solid Shapes → Dini's Surface
children.description: A constant-negative-curvature surface of revolution twisted into a helicoid-like band.

children.label: Higher-Dimensional Shapes
children.path: Geometric Shape → Higher-Dimensional Shapes
children.description: The family of shapes in $n$ dimensions, $n > 3$.

children.label: Polytope
children.path: Geometric Shape → Higher-Dimensional Shapes → Polytope
children.description: A bounded shape whose boundary is made of flat $(n-1)$-faces.

children.label: Simplex
children.path: Geometric Shape → Higher-Dimensional Shapes → Polytope → Simplex
children.description: $\Delta^n$: $n+1$ affinely independent vertices — the smallest shape in its dimension.

children.label: Hypercube
children.path: Geometric Shape → Higher-Dimensional Shapes → Polytope → Hypercube
children.description: The product of $n$ intervals — the tesseract in four dimensions.

children.label: Tesseract
children.path: Geometric Shape → Higher-Dimensional Shapes → Polytope → Hypercube → Tesseract
children.description: The 4-cube: eight cubical cells, and the projection every 4-D drawing shows.

children.label: Cross-Polytope
children.path: Geometric Shape → Higher-Dimensional Shapes → Polytope → Cross-Polytope
children.description: The $n$-dimensional octahedron, dual to the hypercube.

children.label: Regular Polytope
children.path: Geometric Shape → Higher-Dimensional Shapes → Polytope → Regular Polytope
children.description: The finite list of regular shapes per dimension: five in 3-D, six in 4-D, three above.

children.label: 24-Cell
children.path: Geometric Shape → Higher-Dimensional Shapes → Polytope → Regular Polytope → 24-Cell
children.description: The icositetrachoron: 24 octahedral cells, self-dual, and the only regular polytope with no analogue in another dimension.

children.label: 120-Cell
children.path: Geometric Shape → Higher-Dimensional Shapes → Polytope → Regular Polytope → 120-Cell
children.description: The hecatonicosachoron: 120 dodecahedral cells, the 4-D counterpart of the dodecahedron.

children.label: 600-Cell
children.path: Geometric Shape → Higher-Dimensional Shapes → Polytope → Regular Polytope → 600-Cell
children.description: The hexacosichoron: 600 tetrahedral cells, dual to the 120-cell.

children.label: Demihypercube
children.path: Geometric Shape → Higher-Dimensional Shapes → Polytope → Demihypercube
children.description: The hypercube with alternate vertices removed — the $n$-demicube, and the 16-cell in four dimensions.

children.label: Hypersimplex
children.path: Geometric Shape → Higher-Dimensional Shapes → Polytope → Hypersimplex
children.description: The polytope between the simplex and the hypercube: vertices with exactly $k$ ones.

children.label: Duoprism
children.path: Geometric Shape → Higher-Dimensional Shapes → Polytope → Duoprism
children.description: The product of two polygons — the 4-D shape whose cells are prisms.

children.label: Duocylinder
children.path: Geometric Shape → Higher-Dimensional Shapes → Polytope → Duocylinder
children.description: The product of two disks — the 4-D shape that rolls in two independent directions.

children.label: Hypercone
children.path: Geometric Shape → Higher-Dimensional Shapes → Polytope → Hypercone
children.description: The cone over a sphere: the 4-D analogue of the solid cone.

children.label: Zonotope
children.path: Geometric Shape → Higher-Dimensional Shapes → Polytope → Zonotope
children.description: The Minkowski sum of segments — the polytope whose every 2-face is centrally symmetric.

children.label: Permutohedron
children.path: Geometric Shape → Higher-Dimensional Shapes → Polytope → Permutohedron
children.description: The convex hull of the permutations of a point — the polytope whose vertices are orderings.

children.label: Associahedron
children.path: Geometric Shape → Higher-Dimensional Shapes → Polytope → Associahedron
children.description: The polytope whose vertices are the bracketings of a product, edges the associativity moves.

children.label: Ball
children.path: Geometric Shape → Higher-Dimensional Shapes → Ball
children.description: The points within a radius of a centre — the filled hypersphere.

children.label: Hypersphere
children.path: Geometric Shape → Higher-Dimensional Shapes → Hypersphere
children.description: The boundary of the ball; its two-dimensional shadow is the ordinary sphere.

children.label: 3-Sphere
children.path: Geometric Shape → Higher-Dimensional Shapes → Hypersphere → 3-Sphere
children.description: The glome: the hypersphere in four dimensions, and the set of unit quaternions.

children.label: N-Torus
children.path: Geometric Shape → Higher-Dimensional Shapes → N-Torus
children.description: The product of $n$ circles — genus $n$-fold, and the phase space of $n$ independent oscillators.

children.label: Shape Arrangements
children.path: Geometric Shape → Shape Arrangements
children.description: The family of figures that are shape sets: several shapes read together rather than one connected shape.

children.label: Compound Shape
children.path: Geometric Shape → Shape Arrangements → Compound Shape
children.description: Two or more shapes joined or superposed — a cross, a fan of segments, a union of disks.

children.label: Cross
children.path: Geometric Shape → Shape Arrangements → Compound Shape → Cross
children.description: Two orthogonal bars — the plus sign as a figure, and the Greek cross as a polygon.

children.label: Yin-Yang
children.path: Geometric Shape → Shape Arrangements → Compound Shape → Yin-Yang
children.description: The taijitu: two congruent interlocking halves, each carrying the other's seed.

children.label: Stellated Octahedron
children.path: Geometric Shape → Shape Arrangements → Compound Shape → Stellated Octahedron
children.description: Two tetrahedra interpenetrating — the compound that is also a stellation.

children.label: Compound of Cube and Octahedron
children.path: Geometric Shape → Shape Arrangements → Compound Shape → Compound of Cube and Octahedron
children.description: The two dual Platonic solids inscribed in one another, their edges bisecting at right angles.

children.label: Tessellation
children.path: Geometric Shape → Shape Arrangements → Tessellation
children.description: Shapes covering the plane with no gaps and no overlaps: regular, Archimedean, or aperiodic.

children.label: Regular Tessellation
children.path: Geometric Shape → Shape Arrangements → Tessellation → Regular Tessellation
children.description: One regular polygon, repeated — the three tilings by triangle, square, and hexagon.

children.label: Archimedean Tessellation
children.path: Geometric Shape → Shape Arrangements → Tessellation → Archimedean Tessellation
children.description: More than one regular polygon at every vertex — the eight uniform tilings.

children.label: Voronoi Diagram
children.path: Geometric Shape → Shape Arrangements → Tessellation → Voronoi Diagram
children.description: The partition into nearest-site regions — the shape a point set induces on the plane.

children.label: Delaunay Triangulation
children.path: Geometric Shape → Shape Arrangements → Tessellation → Delaunay Triangulation
children.description: The triangulation whose circumcircles are empty — the Voronoi diagram's dual.

children.label: Aperiodic Tessellation
children.path: Geometric Shape → Shape Arrangements → Tessellation → Aperiodic Tessellation
children.description: A tiling with no translational symmetry — the shapes that tile only without repeating.

children.label: Penrose Tiling
children.path: Geometric Shape → Shape Arrangements → Tessellation → Aperiodic Tessellation → Penrose Tiling
children.description: Two rhombi, five-fold symmetry, and no period — the quasicrystal pattern.

children.label: Packing
children.path: Geometric Shape → Shape Arrangements → Packing
children.description: Shapes placed without overlap but not required to cover — circles, spheres, and their densest arrangements.

children.label: Circle Packing
children.path: Geometric Shape → Shape Arrangements → Packing → Circle Packing
children.description: Disks placed without overlap: the hexagonal arrangement is the densest.

children.label: Sphere Packing
children.path: Geometric Shape → Shape Arrangements → Packing → Sphere Packing
children.description: Balls placed without overlap — the Kepler conjecture's subject.

children.label: Hexagonal Close Packing
children.path: Geometric Shape → Shape Arrangements → Packing → Sphere Packing → Hexagonal Close Packing
children.description: The densest sphere packing: $\pi/(3\sqrt{2}) \approx 0.74$ of space filled.

children.label: Shape Properties
children.path: Geometric Shape → Shape Properties
children.description: Predicates asserted of a shape rather than figures beside it.

children.label: Dimension
children.path: Geometric Shape → Shape Properties → Dimension
children.description: The $n$ of the ambient space the figure lives in — the predicate that decides which figure families the shape admits.

children.label: Convexity
children.path: Geometric Shape → Shape Properties → Convexity
children.description: Every segment joining two of its points stays inside the figure — the predicate that separates the convex family from the concave and the star kinds.

children.label: Regularity
children.path: Geometric Shape → Shape Properties → Regularity
children.description: All sides and all angles equal where the figure has them — the predicate that singles out the regular member of each family.

children.label: Self-Intersection
children.path: Geometric Shape → Shape Properties → Self-Intersection
children.description: Whether the boundary meets itself — the predicate that separates the simple figure from the crossed and the star kinds.

children.label: Orientability
children.path: Geometric Shape → Shape Properties → Orientability
children.description: Whether a consistent side can be chosen — the predicate that separates the sphere from the Möbius strip and the Klein bottle.

children.label: Boundedness
children.path: Geometric Shape → Shape Properties → Boundedness
children.description: Whether the figure fits inside a ball of finite radius — the predicate that separates the segment from the ray and the line.

children.label: Connectedness
children.path: Geometric Shape → Shape Properties → Connectedness
children.description: Whether the figure is one piece — the predicate that separates a single figure from a compound or an arrangement.

children.label: Complexity
children.path: Geometric Shape → Shape Properties → Complexity
children.description: The description length of the figure's generating rule — the predicate that separates the circle from the Koch curve at equal extent.
